questions.q: Why does Driftwood's dashboard use Import mode instead of DirectQuery?
options: The actual requirement is a daily number, not a live one -- Import's snapshot-and-refresh model fits that requirement better than re-querying Snowflake on every click
DirectQuery cannot connect to Snowflake at all
Import mode is always the objectively superior choice for every Power BI report
Snowflake does not support DirectQuery connections
questions.explain: The choice follows directly from the stated business requirement (daily refresh), not a blanket preference for Import over DirectQuery.

questions.q: Which Snowflake objects does Power BI actually connect to in this capstone?
options: Only the marts: fct_subscriptions and dim_subscribers
The raw billing_events and usage_events tables directly
The int_subscriber_activity intermediate model
All layers simultaneously -- raw, intermediate, and marts
questions.explain: Power BI connects only to the tested, documented mart tables -- never raw or intermediate models, which haven't been validated by dbt's tests.

questions.q: Why would connecting Power BI directly to raw.billing_events undermine Lesson 5's testing and documentation work?
options: It would bypass every dbt test and every grain/column documentation the marts layer was specifically built to provide before data reaches a report
Raw tables are physically inaccessible to Power BI
It would have no real effect since raw and marts contain identical data
Power BI cannot technically connect to any table outside the marts schema
questions.explain: The marts layer is where dbt's tests and documentation actually apply -- connecting upstream of that bypasses all the quality guarantees this project built.

questions.q: Why is Power BI's scheduled refresh set to 7 AM, one hour after the Airflow DAG's 6 AM start?
options: To give the full load/transform/test sequence time to finish, avoiding a refresh that captures the marts mid-build
7 AM is Power BI's only available scheduled refresh time
The one-hour gap has no real purpose and is arbitrary
Airflow requires exactly one hour between DAG start and any downstream refresh
questions.explain: The buffer is a deliberate decision based on how long the DAG's sequence takes -- refreshing too early risks showing an incomplete or inconsistent snapshot.

questions.q: What would happen if Power BI refreshed at 6:05 AM instead of 7 AM?
options: It could capture the marts mid-build, partway through dbt_run, showing leadership an incomplete or inconsistent number with no indication anything was wrong
The refresh would simply fail with a clear error message
Nothing different would happen -- the timing has no effect on data consistency
Power BI would automatically wait for the DAG to finish before refreshing
questions.explain: A too-early refresh risks silently capturing a half-updated state -- the dangerous failure mode the one-hour buffer is specifically designed to avoid.
